title: Keyboard Navigation
description: Understand keyboard accessibility requirements for web applications.

options.text: All interactive elements should be reachable and operable via keyboard alone
options.explanation: WCAG 2.1.1 requires all functionality to be available via keyboard. This means proper tab order, Enter/Space to activate, Escape to dismiss, arrow keys for composite widgets, and visible focus indicators.

options.text: tabindex='0' makes an element the first item in the tab order
options.explanation: tabindex='0' puts an element in the natural tab order (based on DOM position). tabindex='1' or higher sets a specific order (but is considered an anti-pattern — use DOM order instead).

options.text: Removing the default focus outline improves accessibility
options.explanation: The focus outline is critical for keyboard users to know which element is focused. If you remove it for aesthetics, you MUST provide an alternative visible focus indicator. :focus-visible helps — it shows focus rings only for keyboard navigation.

options.text: Mouse-only interactions are acceptable for non-essential features
options.explanation: WCAG requires ALL interactive features to be keyboard-accessible, not just 'essential' ones. Hover-only menus, drag-only interfaces, and click-only controls all need keyboard alternatives.
